Washing your hands is a basic hygiene practice that helps prevent the spread of illnesses and infections. When you don't wash your hands, especially after they've come into contact with dirt, germs, or other contaminants, you risk transferring those germs to your food and then into your body. This can lead to a range of health problems, from mild stomach upset to more serious illnesses. It's generally considered a good practice to wash your hands with soap and water before eating, preparing food, or engaging in any activity that involves handling food or your face. This simple habit can go a long way in maintaining good health and preventing the spread of illnesses.
